# Browser OAuth connection and troubleshooting

OAuth is the default. Add the MCP URL, sign in to this instance in the browser, and explicitly confirm selected scopes. The client receives tokens automatically. Personal/service API Keys remain an advanced compatibility option; OpenAPI, App SDK and CLI authentication stays unchanged.

## Codex

```bash
codex mcp add tier0-uns --url "<MCP_URL>"
```

add starts browser authorization. After completing it, use /mcp to inspect tools; a second login is unnecessary. Use `codex mcp login tier0-uns` only if no browser opened, authorization expired, or you need different scopes. Scope changes may use `--scopes`, for example `uns.read,uns.source,uns.stream,uns.app.read,offline_access`.

Choose Read / Write / All in the consent page. Read includes available requested query scopes; Write adds create/update but excludes deletion; All additionally includes requested archive/delete access. Presets never expand the request or user permissions. Write is unavailable when no writing scope was requested or can be granted.

New connections discover candidate scopes through protected-resource metadata. Consent still defaults to Read; writing requires selecting Write / All explicitly. An omitted scope uses the client's registered ceiling; an explicit read-only request remains read-only. The page distinguishes a read-only client request from missing account write permissions. Remove and re-add a connection if the client cached a read-only registration; existing grants and refresh tokens never gain writes automatically. The initial-password reminder is hidden during MCP consent and its login redirect, while normal platform pages retain it.

Desktop and CLI share configuration on the same host. Both the client and browser must reach the instance; the callback returns to the client computer. Localhost does not identify another server. Use HTTPS for remote/production access; loopback HTTP works for local development. Trusted proxy prefixes and MCP_PUBLIC_URL determine the deployed endpoint.

## Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope local tier0-uns "<MCP_URL>"
claude mcp get tier0-uns
```

Use /mcp in a session to authenticate through the browser. A separate command-line OAuth login depends on the installed client version; older releases have no such subcommand. DCR works without fetching cloud-hosted CIMD.

## Generic clients

Use Streamable HTTP with protected-resource/authorization-server discovery, public-client DCR and S256 PKCE. Default configuration includes the URL only. This release registers local loopback callbacks with exact host/path and variable ports.

## Scopes and revocation

uns.read reads UNS models, Records and Samples. Model/data/Source/Stream/App management and deletion use separate unchecked scopes; see write.en-US.md. Optional uns.source, uns.stream and uns.app.read cover redacted Source/Stream and App Collection grants. offline_access only enables refresh. Effective access intersects current user permissions with consented scopes, never inferred role names. Revoke your connection from API Key management or the standard revocation endpoint. Access tokens expire quickly, refresh tokens rotate, and reuse revokes the grant.

## Advanced API Key compatibility

```powershell
$env:TIER0_API_KEY = "<API_KEY>"
codex mcp add tier0-uns-key --url "<MCP_URL>" --bearer-token-env-var TIER0_API_KEY
```

X-API-Key: <API_KEY> also works. Copy a clear key at creation; masked values cannot authenticate. Never put keys in URLs or shared configuration. App-bound keys keep their existing SDK/OpenAPI path.

| Symptom | Action |
| --- | --- |
| 401 | Reauthenticate expired/revoked OAuth, or check the API Key. A platform session is not an MCP access token |
| 403 / missing tools | Check current permissions and granted optional read scopes |
| invalid_scope | Refresh scope expansion is not supported; request and explicitly consent to additional scopes through a new login |
| invalid_grant | The code expired/was consumed, PKCE/redirect/resource mismatched, or refresh rotated; authorize again |
| https_required | Remote/production access requires HTTPS; local loopback HTTP is supported |
| Consent request invalid | Start, sign in and consent in the same browser; restart expired/processed requests |
| 503 / disabled | Check MCP_ENABLED and backend health using the deployment workflow |
| GET/DELETE 405 | Stateless MCP uses POST JSON-RPC, not a GET event stream |
| RESULT_TOO_LARGE | Reduce size/include/queries; do not treat truncated data as complete |

Endpoint availability never means a client is connected.
